edits.value_json: 爸 is absent from Shuowen. A Guangya entry groups 爸 with 爹 and 㸙 under the gloss “father”; this records use of the word, not when the graph was formed. The selected redraws show 父 and 巴 separately, not earlier forms or a sequence for 爸.

One historical dictionary preserves an account in which 父 was added to a father word written 八八 or 巴巴. A later study instead argues that the father word is phonologically from 父. These competing explanations do not establish how or when the graph was formed.
